why: Each campus's mode-of-study split adds to 100%, and campuses of 8,000 to 26,000 students growing 1% to 7% a year are believable for a private university group.
A dealership group with about $500 million in revenue, thin new-car margins of 3-5% and servicing margins around 30% matches how car retailers report.
About 400,000 calls a month for an electricity supplier is believable, and the voice-menu funnel shrinks at each stage as it must (63% to 60% to 52%, and 55% to 50% to 39%).
Revenue of $330-565 million against markets of $1.4-2.6 billion gives a share of roughly 22%, and about $6 million of revenue per sales rep is believable for farm machinery.
Profit equals revenue minus costs in both columns, and about $1.80 of revenue per kg of linen at roughly 125 tonnes a day is believable for a large industrial laundry.

A fast-growing meat-substitute start-up with revenue rising from €19 million to €124 million and deep but narrowing losses (-161% to -26%) is extreme but possible for a business that has never made a profit.
The table adds up to about 1.1 million staff in one metro area, with most not yet contacted, which is believable for a city-wide B2B app.
Every score distribution adds to 100%, and 40,000 survey responses split 26,000 to 14,000 is believable for a mass-market toothbrush launch.
2.2 million smoothies across 120 bars is about 50 a day per bar, and 0.15 kg of pulp at $2-5 per kg is a believable ingredient cost.
Salaries at 72% and project expenses at 37% of €212 million in fees add to 109%, which matches the stated loss and is possible for a struggling consultancy.
